Burning it to the face at 20 life wastes a removal spell for negligible value.

annotations.description: The opponent cast Into the Flood Maw targeting KimiK2 Valley's Otter Token (which was the opponent's Stormchaser's Talent token on their board - wait, looking more carefully, the Otter Token is on Kimi25 Truth's battlefield). Actually, re-reading: Into the Flood Maw returns a creature an opponent controls to hand - so it's targeting something KimiK2 Valley controls. But KimiK2 Valley has no creatures on the battlefield. The Otter Token is on Kimi25 Truth's side. Wait - the result says 'KimiK2 Valley puts Otter Token from battlefield into its owner's hand' - this means the opponent bounced the Otter Token back to its owner's (Kimi25 Truth's) hand, but it was on Kimi25 Truth's battlefield. Actually, looking at the After line, Into the Flood Maw was gifted (Fish token created) and used to bounce the Otter Token. Since the gift was promised, it returns a nonland permanent - the opponent bounced their own Otter Token? No - Into the Flood Maw says 'return target creature an opponent controls' or with gift 'return target nonland permanent an opponent controls.' KimiK2 Valley has no creatures/nonland permanents visible. Wait - actually I don't think KimiK2 Valley had a choice here. The opponent was casting Into the Flood Maw and KimiK2 Valley could respond with Bounce Off or Burst Lightning. The key question is: could KimiK2 Valley have responded productively? They could have cast Burst Lightning targeting the Otter Token (1/1 prowess) to kill it before it gets bounced back to hand. By not responding, the opponent gets to rebuy the Otter Token to hand (it's a token, so it ceases to exist - actually tokens that return to hand cease to exist). So the bounce actually removes the Otter Token permanently. This means the opponent is spending a card to remove their own token, which is bad for them. KimiK2 Valley was correct to let it resolve - no blunder here.
